domain_reasoning: The reviewer reads a specification, test plan or design document and writes comments, with little other software to operate.
length_reasoning: A short change note or small spec takes about 20 minutes; a typical requirements or design document takes an hour; a long specification with compliance checks takes several hours.
review_reasoning: The author or QA lead reads the findings against the document: a short one is quick, a typical one needs several findings checked in context, a long one needs many findings verified against the source text.
stakes_reasoning: A missed inaccuracy or gap usually surfaces later in development or testing and is fixed in a revision, though a compliance gap can cost more.
context_reasoning: Judging accuracy and completeness needs knowledge of the product, its requirements and the team's standards, built over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The time goes into reading the account and case notes, composing the message, and sending and logging it in the CRM or billing system, with the writing itself a smaller part.
length_reasoning: A routine reply from a template takes about 5 minutes; a claim result or adjustment notice needing the case file checked takes around 15; a sensitive or complex case takes 40 minutes.
review_reasoning: A supervisor or QA reviewer reads the message against the account record: a template reply is quick, a typical one needs the facts checked, a complex one needs the case history read.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong statement reaches the customer and causes a follow-up call or complaint, but can be corrected with another message; a wrong claim decision or adjustment can have financial effect.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's policies, tone conventions, templates and account systems, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up rates, entering the charge and taking payment or setting up billing in the billing or point-of-sale system.
length_reasoning: A simple quote and payment takes a few minutes; a service needing a deposit, a payment plan or billing setup takes ten to twenty.
review_reasoning: A reviewer checks the recorded contact and the billing entry against the rate schedule, or reconciliation compares totals; longer contacts take a little longer to follow.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong charge or misapplied payment is money handled directly and may be found only at reconciliation or by customer complaint, but is usually correctable by adjustment.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's rate schedules, deposit rules and billing system, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into pulling data from test management and CI tools and working with it in spreadsheets or scripts, then writing up the findings, so operating tools outweighs writing.
length_reasoning: A quick trend check on one suite takes a couple of hours; a typical report across releases takes about half a day; a large cross-project analysis takes two days.
review_reasoning: The QA manager reads the report and checks the key trends and data pulls: a short one is quick, a typical one needs spot-checks of the numbers, a large one needs the method and data traced.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong trend or recommendation can misdirect test effort but is caught over time and revised.
context_reasoning: Interpreting results and test history needs months of knowing this product's test suites, flaky tests and release history.

domain_reasoning: The worker gathers examples from case records and writes a recommendation memo, so reading and writing text dominates.
length_reasoning: A short note on a small recurring issue takes about 45 minutes; a typical recommendation with examples takes two hours; a well-evidenced proposal needing data gathering takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A supervisor or process owner reads the recommendation and checks a sample of the examples against records; a longer proposal needs more examples and the reasoning checked.
stakes_reasoning: A weak recommendation is usually declined or revised; acting on a wrong one could waste effort but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the employer's processes, products and who owns what, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Besides listening, the time goes into entering complaint details into the case or CRM system.
length_reasoning: A simple complaint takes a few minutes; typical ones about eight; an upset customer or a complicated complaint takes twenty or more.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the recorded call and checks the case entry captures the details; longer calls take proportionally longer.
stakes_reasoning: Missing or wrong details cause rework, a repeat contact or an unhappy customer, but are recoverable by calling back.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's complaint procedures and system, learned within a few weeks.

unit_flag_reason: A testing tool or framework component ranges from a small helper script to a substantial framework module, so the item mixes very different sizes of work.
domain_reasoning: The work is writing and testing code, plus handling code review.
length_reasoning: A small utility or helper takes a day; a typical framework component takes a few days; a substantial tool takes a couple of weeks of active work.
review_reasoning: A code reviewer reads the change and runs it: a small utility is quick, a typical component needs a careful read and a trial run, a large tool needs a long review across files.
stakes_reasoning: Bugs in a test tool cause false results or flaky runs, found within the team and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's codebase, test infrastructure and conventions, which take months to learn.

domain_reasoning: The work is in monitoring consoles, system tools and ticketing, checking and acting on the problem.
length_reasoning: Many alerts are known or transient and closed in minutes; a real slowdown needing investigation and a fix takes an hour or more.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the closing note and glances at the evidence; a typical item needs the cause checked; a long one needs its steps followed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed alert usually recurs and is caught, but a missed real fault can affect many users or cause an outage.
context_reasoning: Telling normal from abnormal needs months of familiarity with this environment's systems and history.

domain_reasoning: The work is configuring the application or writing macros and scripts, which is mostly changing configuration or code.
length_reasoning: A template tweak takes under an hour; a typical macro or configuration change with testing takes half a day; a more involved script with user testing takes more than a day.
review_reasoning: The supervisor or users check that the change works and does not break anything: a small one takes a quick trial, a typical one needs a test walkthrough, a complex script needs a closer look at the code and edge cases.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty customization affects users and needs rework but is usually reversible by rolling back.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's applications, existing customizations and users' working practices, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into running the software, observing it and capturing performance data and notes on site, then writing findings, which is mostly operating applications and tools.
length_reasoning: A short visit with a few measurements takes half a day; a typical evaluation with write-up takes a day or two; a multi-day evaluation at a complex site takes much longer.
review_reasoning: The test lead reads the findings and checks the main observations against the data or logs; a short report is quick, a typical one needs data checks, a long one needs many observations traced.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong findings may misdirect fixes or hide a defect, but beta feedback is iterative and can be corrected before release.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and its expected behavior and the particular beta customer, built over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: The work is installing and configuring a tool through installers, consoles and settings, with some scripting.
length_reasoning: A simple tool upgrade takes under an hour; a typical install with configuration takes a few hours; a complex install with integrations and server setup takes a day or more.
review_reasoning: A QA lead or user checks that the tool starts and works with the team's projects: a simple upgrade is a quick smoke test, a typical install needs integrations checked, a complex one needs a longer check of configuration.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty install blocks or disrupts the team's testing but is fixed or rolled back quickly.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's environments, integrations and conventions, learned in a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is provisioning and configuring servers, databases and network settings through consoles, scripts and deployment tools.
length_reasoning: A small, simple environment takes a day; a typical production-like environment takes several days; a large multi-tier environment takes a couple of weeks of active work.
review_reasoning: The performance testers check the environment against the production specification: a small one needs a quick comparison, a typical one needs configuration verified item by item, a large one needs a long walkthrough and test runs.
stakes_reasoning: A mismatch with production makes performance results misleading, which can lead to wrong release decisions, though it is usually found when results look odd.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the production architecture, configuration and tooling, which takes months to build.

domain_reasoning: The worker trials candidate tools, reads vendor material and writes a recommendation; the trial is software use, but the reading and writing take most of the time.
length_reasoning: A quick comparison of two tools takes a day; a typical evaluation with a trial takes a week of part-time work; a major selection with a pilot takes a few weeks.
review_reasoning: The QA manager reads the recommendation and checks the key criteria and claims: a short comparison is quick, a typical evaluation needs the criteria and some trial results checked, a major one needs the whole case read.
stakes_reasoning: A poor tool choice costs licence money and team time and is hard to reverse once adopted, though it is typically a moderate loss.
context_reasoning: Judging fit needs knowledge of the team's workflow, existing tools and needs, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The time goes into reading applications, interviewing and writing up an assessment, with interviews counted as part of the work; reading and writing text outweighs systems use.
length_reasoning: A vacancy with few applicants takes about six hours across screening and interviews; a typical one takes a couple of days; one with many applicants takes several days of active work.
review_reasoning: HR or the hiring manager reads the recommendation and checks the evidence for the choice and process fairness; a small field is quick, a large one needs more candidates' notes read.
stakes_reasoning: A poor hire is costly and hard to reverse, and a flawed process can expose the employer to legal risk.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the team's work, HR process and the people involved, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up account, billing and usage records in the customer system.
length_reasoning: A simple lookup that explains a charge takes a few minutes; typical ones eight; a dispute needing history and usage comparison takes twenty.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recording and checks the account facts and explanation; longer calls take longer to follow.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong assessment leads to an unjustified rejection or credit, which causes a complaint or small financial loss but can be revisited.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's billing rules, systems and typical causes of bill issues, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running installers, applying settings and patches and updating the ticket on the user's machine, which is operating applications.
length_reasoning: A simple reinstall or patch takes about 15 minutes; typical installs with setup take 30; a troublesome repair takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: The support lead or user checks that the software runs and the ticket notes match: a simple one is a glance, a typical one needs a short test, a troublesome repair needs the notes and steps checked.
stakes_reasoning: A bad install affects one user and is fixed quickly.
context_reasoning: A skilled outsider with the specification could do it about as fast, apart from learning the ticketing tool.

domain_reasoning: The work is in monitoring tools, logs, profilers and test runs to find the cause of the anomaly.
length_reasoning: Many issues are known or quickly explained in under half an hour; real performance problems take hours of tracing to a cause.
review_reasoning: A test lead or developer reads the findings and checks the evidence: a quick one is a glance at the graphs, a typical one needs the cause checked against logs, a long one needs the chain of reasoning followed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed issue usually reappears and is caught, but a missed real bottleneck can reach production and cause slowdowns or outages.
context_reasoning: Judging what is anomalous needs months of knowledge of this system's architecture, normal behavior and history.
